answer: Bind each identity to one hardware-backed key. A secure enclave issues a crystal attestation proving the key was born inside a single physical device and cannot be copied. Independent registries mirror the attestation, so one device trying to mint a second identity shows up at once as a duplicate. Re-attestation moves at a glacier pace, allowed only after a long cooling interval, so stolen hardware cannot be spun into fresh clones quickly. An honest agent pays for one attestation; an attacker must buy one real device per fake identity.
